description: Add daily aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg as home medications
presentation: A 63-year-old man with hypertension and CAD underwent CABG two months ago and developed postoperative delirium. His home medications include aspirin 81 mg daily and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Today, despite orientation to person, place, and time and a normal neurologic exam in clinic, he continues to endorse intermittent confusion, delusions, and paranoid thinking. A noncontrast head CT on last month showed no acute infarct. The patient has no prior history of dementia or psychiatric illness. What is the next best step to evaluate this persistent cognitive deficit?
